turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi, I'm Maeve Gallagher. I'm a licensed clinical social worker, and today is really about getting to know you. Could you start by confirming your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Rashid Al -Aman, February 17, 1974.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thanks, Rashid. And is 216 -555 -0139 still a good number for you?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, that's my cell. Great.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So what made you decide to come in? Honestly,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: my wife Samira pushed me. I got laid off 6 weeks ago. 19 years at Tri -County Logistics I ran warehouse operations and one Tuesday they just called me in and that was it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: 19 years.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's a big loss.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How have you been feeling since then?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Down mostly, kind of useless. And I'm short with the kids which isn't me. I worry about money all the time, the mortgage, my son starting college next year.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What does a typical day look like right now?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I sleep until 10, which I never did. I send out a few applications, then I'm on the couch. I stopped going to my Saturday basketball with the guys.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I just don't want to explain it.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: How's your appetite? I'm eating more honestly, junk mostly. And before the layoff,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: how were you doing? Any time in your life you felt like this?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I was fine.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I've never seen a counselor or anything before this. Any panic attacks, or feeling like your heart is racing and you can't breathe.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, not that, more like a knot in my stomach. What about alcohol,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: smoking, any other substances?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I don't drink, I smoked for years but I quit ten years ago when my daughter was born, nothing else.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good for you on the quitting. I'm going to ask you something I ask everyone. Have you had any thoughts of ending your life or of hurting yourself? No, no, I'd never do that to my family. Any thoughts of hurting anyone else? Maybe your old employer.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Ah, no, I'm angry, but no.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thank you for being straight with me. The two questionnaires you filled out, your PHQ -9 for depression is 11, and your GED -7 for anxiety is 10. So both in the moderate range. And what I'm seeing today, your casually dressed, good eye contact, your speech is normal, your mood sounds down and a bit anxious, and your thinking is clear and logical. That's fair. What's been helping,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: even a little. Walking the dog and Samira, she's been great. She's picking up extra shifts at the hospital though so I feel guilty about that too.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So here's my impression. What you're going through sounds like an adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood. Basically, a strong emotional reaction to a big stressful change, the job loss. It's very common, and it usually responds well to therapy.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, so what do we do?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'd like to meet weekly, about an hour each time. We'll use a CBT approach and work on behavioral activation, which means rebuilding some structure. To start,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I want you up by 7,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: 30 on weekdays, a set two -hour block for jobs searching each morning, and one call to a basketball friend this week.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I can do that, maybe not the basketball call, but I'll try.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Also, Tri -County should have offered outplacement services with your severance. It's worth calling HR to use those. And if Samira wants to join a session later on, that's welcome.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I didn't even think about outplacement.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Before you leave, we'll fill out a short safety plan together. If you ever start having thoughts of hurting yourself, you can call or text 988 anytime, day or night. And if the mood gets worse despite therapy, we can talk about seeing one of our psychiatrists, but I don't think we're there.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Understood.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Our next session is next Thursday, October 1st, at 4 o 'clock.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thursday works thank you Maeve, this helped more than I expected.
